original_question: Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system and let u <= v in W. Must there always exist another Coxeter system (W',S') and an element w in W' such that the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q) can be realized as P_{e,w}(q)?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 1.9 (the Björner problem about realizing an arbitrary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial as one of the form P_{e,w}).
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct target almost verbatim: it asks exactly whether every Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial P_{u,v}(q) can be realized as P_{e,w}(q) in some Coxeter system. It correctly uses a Coxeter system (W,S), elements u,v with u \le v, a second Coxeter system (W',S'), and the target form P_{e,w}(q).
missing_details: The order relation u \le v should be stated to be the Bruhat order.

Because the paper first introduces parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, it is better to specify that P_{u,v}(q) denotes the ordinary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial, i.e. P_{u,v}=P^{\emptyset,-1}_{u,v}=P^{\emptyset,q}_{u,v}.
The equality should be stated as an equality of polynomials in Z[q], with q an indeterminate.
The symbol e should be identified as the identity element of W'.

The paper does not require W' to be distinct from W; it asks for some Coxeter system (W',S'). Moreover, it immediately remarks that the answer is negative if one insists on W'=W, so the refined question should avoid wording that suggests this extra restriction.
To be fully stand-alone, the quantifiers should be explicit: for every Coxeter system (W,S) and every pair u,v in W with u \le v in Bruhat order, does such a pair (W',w) exist?
refined_question: Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system, let u,v \in W with u \le v in the Bruhat order, and let P_{u,v}(q) \in Z[q] denote the ordinary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial of W (equivalently, P_{u,v}=P^{\emptyset,-1}_{u,v}=P^{\emptyset,q}_{u,v} in the notation of Theorem 1.3). Must there exist a Coxeter system (W',S') and an element w \in W' such that, if e denotes the identity element of W', one has P_{u,v}(q)=P_{e,w}(q)?
justification: The draft is aimed at Problem 1.9 in Section 1. The notation P_{u,v} is fixed by Theorem 1.3 together with the sentence immediately after it, which identifies the ordinary Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials as the J=\emptyset specialization. The paragraph immediately before Problem 1.9 gives the motivating realization result for arbitrary polynomials P(q) \in N[q] with P(0)=1, and Problem 1.9 then asks whether one can always realize such a polynomial in the more special form P_{e,w}. The remark immediately after Problem 1.9 is important paper-context: the answer is obviously negative if one additionally requires W'=W. So your draft is substantively correct, but it needs the Bruhat-order clarification, the ordinary-versus-parabolic notation clarification, the role of e, the ring Z[q], and the avoidance of the unintended extra restriction that W' be a different system.
